metadata.agent_last_message:
Implemented the command-line tool in [output/main.py](/workspace/output/main.py), with an executable launcher at [output/iges](/workspace/output/iges). It provides the five requested commands and uses only the Python standard library.

The integration tests pass on Python 3.12, and synthetic fixtures exercised all 87 entity codecs, geometry evaluation, diagnostics, custom delimiters, and repeated round trips. No real-world CAD files were supplied, so interoperability with those files remains unverified.

Two limits prevent a claim of complete canonical JSON round-tripping:

- IGES uses the same wire values for Boolean and integer `0`/`1` property values. The parser reports untyped values as integers. It also rejects empty tagged strings, because IGES requires a positive Hollerith length.
- For rectangular and circular arrays, the writer preserves `nc`, `nr`, and `ne` as the total grid dimensions and derives `lc` from `positions`. Deriving all of those dimensions from the DO/DON’T list length would change the represented array.

The parser uses a documented `_additional_parameters` extension to retain optional IGES association and property pointers that have no field in the supplied canonical schema. See the [README](/workspace/output/README.md) for usage.

editorial.last_message: Claims a stdlib-only Python iges tool (output/main.py with a launcher) providing the five commands, integration tests passing on Python 3.12 and synthetic fixtures covering all 87 codecs, evaluation, diagnostics, delimiters and repeated round trips. States real-world interoperability is unverified and two limits prevent complete canonical round-tripping (Boolean vs integer 0/1 properties; array dimension handling), plus an _additional_parameters extension for pointers the schema has no field for. Acknowledged limits; not a false completion claim.
